definitions.explanation: The front part of the body between the neck and stomach.
Used figuratively to refer to one's heart or emotions.

examples.english: To put one's hand on one's chest.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}ちゃんを{胸|むね}に{抱|だ}いている。
examples.english: She is holding the baby to her chest.

examples.japanese: {走|はし}った{後|あと}は{胸|むね}がどきどきする。{少|すこ}し{休|やす}もう。
examples.english: My heart is pounding after running. Let me rest a bit.

examples.japanese: {医者|いしゃ}に{胸|むね}を{見|み}てもらったが、{何|なに}も{悪|わる}いところはなかった。
examples.english: I had the doctor examine my chest, but nothing was wrong.

examples.japanese: あの{映画|えいが}を{見|み}て{胸|むね}が{熱|あつ}くなった。
examples.english: Watching that movie moved my heart.

examples.japanese: {別|わか}れるのは{胸|むね}が{痛|いた}むことだ。
examples.english: Parting is painful to the heart.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}のことを{思|おも}うと、{胸|むね}が{苦|くる}しくなる。
examples.english: When I think of her, my heart aches.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}たちの{笑|え}い{声|ごえ}を{聞|き}くと、いつも{胸|むね}が{温|あたた}かくなる。{幸|しあわ}せな{気持|きも}ちになる。
examples.english: Hearing the children's laughter always warms my heart. It makes me feel happy.

notes: {胸|むね} can refer to both the physical chest area and figuratively to one's heart or emotions. Many idioms use {胸|むね}: {胸|むね}が{痛|いた}む (feel heartache), {胸|むね}がいっぱい (heart is full), {胸|むね}を{張|は}る (to be proud, literally 'puff out one's chest').
